references.text: Addresses treachery (מַעַל) against the Lord and guilt requiring atonement, using the same terminology for sin against God.
Uses the same expression 'למעל מעל ביהוה' (to act treacherously against the Lord) and describes a guilt offering for unintentional sin.
The same expression 'מעל מעל' is used regarding treachery against the Lord.
Continuation of the same text that elaborates on what treachery against the Lord entails.
Achan's sin is described as 'מעל' (treachery) against the Lord, using the same terminology.
Achan's treachery (מעל) against the Lord is mentioned as an example of sin that affects the entire community.
King Uzziah's treachery (מעל) against the Lord which led to his punishment.
Uses מעל regarding Israel's treachery against God through mixed marriages.
The principle of individual responsibility: 'the one who sins shall die' - parallel to 'הנפש ההוא' (that person) who becomes guilty.
Paul's teaching that all, both men and women, have sinned against God - universal guilt as in 'איש או אשה'.
Encouragement to confess sins to one another, linked to the confession of guilt in Num 5:7.
